claims.claim: Quillbot-paraphrased ChatGPT text was detected with only 26% accuracy.
claims.source: Weber-Wulff, Anohina-Naumeca, Bjelobaba, Foltýnek, Guerrero-Dib, Popoola, Šigut, Waddington — 'Testing of detection tools for AI-generated text' (International Journal for Educational Integrity 19:26, 2023)
claims.quote: The overall accuracy for this case was 26%

claims.claim: Human essays machine-translated into English lost 20 points of accuracy, leaving traces read as AI.
claims.source: Weber-Wulff, Anohina-Naumeca, Bjelobaba, Foltýnek, Guerrero-Dib, Popoola, Šigut, Waddington — 'Testing of detection tools for AI-generated text' (International Journal for Educational Integrity 19:26, 2023)
claims.quote: machine translation leaves some traces of AI in the output

claims.claim: For GPTZero half of positive classifications would be false accusations.
claims.source: Weber-Wulff, Anohina-Naumeca, Bjelobaba, Foltýnek, Guerrero-Dib, Popoola, Šigut, Waddington — 'Testing of detection tools for AI-generated text' (International Journal for Educational Integrity 19:26, 2023)
claims.quote: half of the positive classifications would be false accusations

claims.claim: Translation-driven false positives put second-language students and researchers at risk of false accusation.
claims.source: Weber-Wulff, Anohina-Naumeca, Bjelobaba, Foltýnek, Guerrero-Dib, Popoola, Šigut, Waddington — 'Testing of detection tools for AI-generated text' (International Journal for Educational Integrity 19:26, 2023)
claims.quote: leaving L2 students (and researchers) at risk of being falsely accused

claims.claim: Seven detectors misclassified TOEFL essays at an average 61.22% false-positive rate while US essays passed.
claims.source: Liang, Yuksekgonul, Mao, Wu, Zou — 'GPT detectors are biased against non-native English writers' (Patterns 2023)

claims.claim: Low-perplexity, low-variability human prose is what perplexity detectors penalise.
claims.source: Liang, Yuksekgonul, Mao, Wu, Zou — 'GPT detectors are biased against non-native English writers' (Patterns 2023)
claims.quote: penalize writers with constrained linguistic expressions

claims.claim: A self-edit prompt to use literary language cut detection of GPT essays from 100% to 13%.
claims.source: Liang, Yuksekgonul, Mao, Wu, Zou — 'GPT detectors are biased against non-native English writers' (Patterns 2023)

claims.claim: Detectors caught 39.5% of unmanipulated AI text and mislabelled a third of human controls.
claims.source: Perkins, Roe, Vu, Postma, Hickerson, McGaughran, Khuat — 'GenAI Detection Tools, Adversarial Techniques and Implications for Inclusivity in Higher Education' (IJEI 2024; preprint March 2024)
claims.quote: only 67% of the tests were accurate

claims.feature: spelling errors and burstiness evade detection
claims.claim: Adding spelling errors (12.9%) or varying sentence length (15.9%) made AI text nearly undetectable.
claims.source: Perkins, Roe, Vu, Postma, Hickerson, McGaughran, Khuat — 'GenAI Detection Tools, Adversarial Techniques and Implications for Inclusivity in Higher Education' (IJEI 2024; preprint March 2024)

claims.claim: Across detectors the false-accusation ratio was 15%, up to 50% for the most sensitive tool.
claims.source: Perkins, Roe, Vu, Postma, Hickerson, McGaughran, Khuat — 'GenAI Detection Tools, Adversarial Techniques and Implications for Inclusivity in Higher Education' (IJEI 2024; preprint March 2024)
claims.quote: the rate of false accusations at 15%

claims.claim: The authors warn detectors may unfairly penalise students whose perplexity profile differs, including lower-proficiency writers.
claims.source: Perkins, Roe, Vu, Postma, Hickerson, McGaughran, Khuat — 'GenAI Detection Tools, Adversarial Techniques and Implications for Inclusivity in Higher Education' (IJEI 2024; preprint March 2024)
claims.quote: write at a higher level of perplexity

claims.feature: neurodivergent-writer false positives — NOT FOUND in peer-reviewed literature
claims.claim: No peer-reviewed empirical study measuring detector false positives on autistic, ADHD or dyslexic writers was located (arXiv search, two Crossref queries dry; Semantic Scholar refused); nearest peer-reviewed evidence is Liang 2023 (non-native), Weber-Wulff 2023 (machine-translated L2) and Perkins 2024; Bender et al. 2021 names neurodivergent people only among groups harassed off the platforms that feed training data.
Novelist Jeanette Winterson locates what is beautiful and moving in OpenAI's metafiction story in the story's awareness of its own limits, not in its scene-making or characterisation.
claims.quote: its understanding of its lack of understanding
claims.page: body, paragraph beginning 'What is beautiful and moving'

claims.claim: Winterson rejects the term artificial intelligence in favour of 'alternative intelligence' when defending the OpenAI story.
claims.quote: I think of AI as alternative intelligence

claims.claim: The single passage Winterson reproduces as the story's achievement is the model's statement that it cannot keep its own grief.
claims.source: OpenAI's creative-writing model, quoted by Jeanette Winterson, The Guardian, 12 March 2025
claims.quote: That, perhaps, is my grief: not that I feel loss
